editorial.headline: Other Used-Goods Retail: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers retail sales of used goods that sit outside the specifically defined used-goods categories: nationally open to full foreign ownership, but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is the residual retail home for other used goods: the things bought and sold second-hand that do not fall within the specifically defined used-goods categories of its grouping. It is a retail trade activity, defined by the sale of those goods rather than by a particular product line. That breadth is its practical character: it accommodates used-goods retail that remains within the stated scope without forcing a narrower description than the record supports.

Registration is open across the full business ladder—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. Nationally, the activity is **TERBUKA** to PMA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. The national position is therefore direct: a foreign investor may hold the entire permitted ownership stake in a business registered for this activity, subject to the classification’s stated national position.

Bali changes the answer decisively. A foreigner cannot register this activity through PMA in Bali today. At the Besar scale, every scope within the activity is assessed in OSS as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah risk. That places it inside Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities, reflected in its Bali status of **BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO**.

The distinction matters because the national ceiling and Bali’s registration outcome are not competing descriptions of the same rule. The 100% figure is the national foreign-ownership ceiling. Bali’s result is a location-specific block on PMA registration under its risk-based moratorium. For founders, the honest reading is straightforward: nationally this is fully foreign-open; in Bali, the PMA route is blocked.
